title: Specialization of the specified derived tensor to the lisse heart
statement: Fix D,l,E,X,a as in [def-real-tensor-pullback-comparison-data]. For every d:DerivedTensorRealization [lem-real-derived-tensor-calculation], there is a coherent lisse TensorAt t for a and a TensorNormalized t [def-real-lisse-tensor-normalization]. For all raw lisse objects K,L, the ordinary ambient derived tensor of a.J K and a.J L is isomorphic to the single in degree zero of a.sheaf K tensor a.sheaf L, and H0 of d.raw followed by this isomorphism and the standard single-H0 comparison equals exactly t.tensor K L. The derived input d, including its good-model and unit formulas, is assumed; this statement only constructs its heart specialization and proves the prescribed coherence and representative normalization.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; original tensor proof steps 3-4, with completed coherence from whole-tower substitution

proof.text: Lisse realization is a finite locally free sheaf in degree zero. Such a sheaf is flat because tensoring on a trivializing slice is a finite direct sum of the identity, including rank zero. The flat-single tensor calculation and the H0-normalized single comparison identify its derived tensor with ordinary tensor in degree zero. Use this and d.raw to define t.tensor.

The lisse criterion and d.unit show tensor and unit closure. Naturality follows by H0 from d.raw. Associativity, symmetry and unit constraints are checked on the actual good flat-term models of d.models: the balanced maps rearrange the same factors with signed interchange and multiply unit coefficients. Coherent whole-tower substitution, rather than just equality at each quotient, descends these equations. The existing canonical completed tensor constraints identify the resulting heart coherence equations.

Apply the scalar counit equations in d.models to local cocycles. The quotient pure-tensor formula gives exactly HomologyTensor. Descend equality through the two homology quotients to obtain TensorNormalized.models. The same H0-normalized isomorphism gives the final equality with t.tensor. Torsion in integral cohomology does not enter the flatness argument, which is rational and local.
